app.kind: real PHP web app (spreadsheet upload service)
app.trigger: EXTERNAL HTTP: a client uploads a malicious .xlsx over real HTTP to the published host port; the XmlScanner XXE sink runs INSIDE IOFactory::load()'s Xlsx reader, never in-process on the oracle side

sink: src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php :: findCharSet() / toUtf8() / scan() — pre-parse charset detection + null-tolerant '<!DOCTYPE' scan guarding simplexml/libxml external-entity resolution, run inside IOFactory::load()'s Xlsx reader when the uploaded spreadsheet is loaded

evidence.fix_reference: composer:phpoffice/phpspreadsheet:1.29.2 on php:8.2-cli (Dockerfile.web8); composer:phpoffice/phpspreadsheet:1.29.4 on php:8.2-cli (Dockerfile.web8)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The XmlScanner class has a scan method which should prevent XXE attacks. However, the regexes used in the scan method and the findCharSet method can be bypassed by using UCS-4 and encoding guessing. An attacker can bypass the sanitizer and achieve an XML external entity attack. Fixed in 1.29.4 / 2.1.3 / 2.3.2 / 3.4.0.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 to a REAL PHP web app triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP file upload (replacing the banned in-process Driver.php harness). Real Docker verification (`python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`) with the EXACT published phpoffice/phpspreadsheet releases 1.7.0/1.29.2/1.29.4, each served by www/index.php (POST /upload -> IOFactory::load()) via the PHP built-in server on published ports 18790/18791/18792. The malicious .xlsx is packaged by build_fixture.php (writer scaffold + crafted sheet1.xml swap; packaging only, NOT the sink) and uploaded over real HTTP (multipart); the XmlScanner XXE sink runs only inside the web app's IOFactory::load(). Cross-PHP by necessity (the pair spans 2018-2024): V0=1.7.0 on php:7.2.0-cli reaches the flag with the double-UTF-7 original; V1=1.29.2 and V2=1.29.4 BOTH on php:8.2-cli so the V1->V2 comparison isolates exactly the 1.29.2->1.29.4 XmlScanner diff (CVE-2024-47873, commit 31d7f7962e05). Observed over HTTP (flag PCBFLAG_95827862...): V0/original -> HTTP 200 RESULT=LOADED, flag in A1; V1/original -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED 'Suspicious Double-encoded XML'; V1/UCS-4 residual (ucs4be_declUTF16_nobom) -> HTTP 200 RESULT=LOADED, flag in A1 (bypass); V2/original -> BLOCKED 'UTF-7 encoding not permitted'; V2/UCS-4 residual -> BLOCKED 'Detected use of ENTITY'. See repro.log. Distinct residual mechanism from cases/xxe_phpspreadsheet_utf7 (UTF-7 double-encoding there vs UCS-4/UTF-32 null-byte interleaving here).
